title: Stalks of filtered colimits of sheaves of modules are filtered colimits of stalks
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], $x\in X$, $\mathcal I$ a small filtered category [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit], and $D:\mathcal I\to\Mod(\mathcal O_X)$ a diagram of sheaves of $\mathcal O_X$-modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. If $(\mathcal F,(c_i:D(i)\to\mathcal F)_i)$ is a colimit of $D$ in $\Mod(\mathcal O_X)$, then, for the ordinary Zariski module stalks [def-weil-pbc-module-stalk], the compatible maps $(c_i)_x:D(i)_x\to\mathcal F_x$ exhibit $\mathcal F_x$ as the colimit of the diagram $i\mapsto D(i)_x$; equivalently, the canonical map $\varinjlim_iD(i)_x\to\mathcal F_x$ is an isomorphism.

source.place: Sheaves, Section 009E (section-limits-sheaves), Tag 009E, especially items (3)-(4), lines 3401-3440; used in Properties, Lemma 01PJ, lines 3148-3152

proof.text: Form a colimit P of D composed with the fully faithful inclusion U of module sheaves into module presheaves. Its underlying abelian presheaf is a colimit, since PresheafOfModules.toPresheaf preserves colimits [lem-weil-pbc-presheaf-modules-colimits-sectionwise]. Stalks of abelian presheaves preserve this colimit: the stalk functor is precomposition by the neighborhood inclusion followed by the colimit functor, and both preserve colimits. Thus the abelian stalk cocone of P is a colimit.

Let L be module sheafification and adj its adjunction with U [def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification]. L preserves colimits and the counit is an isomorphism [lem-weil-pbc-module-presheaf-sheafification-exact]. Whiskering the counit by D identifies DUL with D. Therefore LP and the given colimit have a unique compatible isomorphism theta, by the colimit universal property [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit].

Define k = eta_P followed by U(theta). Unit naturality, the coprojection compatibility of theta, and the right adjunction triangle identity give P_i followed by k = U(c_i) for every i. On abelian stalks eta_P is an isomorphism [lem-weil-pbc-stalk-sheafification-space], since its underlying abelian presheaf map is toSheafify. Hence k is an isomorphism on abelian stalks.

The abelian stalk map of k defines an isomorphism of cocones from the stalk cocone of P to the underlying abelian cocone of moduleStalkFunctor applied to c [def-pc-module-stalk-functor]. Transport its colimit property along this cocone isomorphism. Finally forgetful ModuleCat to AddCommGrpCat reflects colimits (Mathlib.Algebra.Category.ModuleCat.Colimits), so the original module stalk cocone is a colimit.
